mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000 thousand units and an elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) indicates a dual stress on demand and monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails when the SPX 20-day return is positive in more than 55% of cases meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining real GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances during GDP contraction periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 thousand persons signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX 20-day returns breaks down with a Rank IC below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and declining retail sales (RSAFS < 350,000 million dollars) indicates stagflationary pressures that trigger equity market sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails when SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.5% in 3 months), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative returns over the next 5 days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances during FEDFUNDS rising cycles.
